name: Common Lisp
note: first de facto specification published in 1984; ANSI standard approved in 1994
typeSystem: Dynamic by default, with declarations that assert types and can enable compiler optimisation; implementations are not generally required to check those assertions. CLOS (the Common Lisp Object System) adds multiple dispatch and multiple inheritance.
runtime: Most implementations compile to native machine code ahead of time or on first use despite the language being dynamically typed; interactive, REPL-driven development is a first-class workflow alongside batch compilation.

runtimes.name: SBCL
runtimes.role: Widely used open-source, high-performance implementation that compiles to native code.

runtimes.name: CCL (Clozure CL)
runtimes.role: Native-code implementation supporting x86-64 on macOS, Linux, and other platforms; currently in limited maintenance.

runtimes.name: CLISP
runtimes.role: Portable bytecode implementation, useful where a native compiler isn't available.

compilers.name: SBCL
compilers.role: High-performance, mostly conforming native-code compiler and interactive environment.

concurrencyModel: Implementation-dependent: SBCL and CCL provide native OS threads; the language standard itself does not mandate a concurrency model.

codeExample.caption: A CLOS class with a generic method
codeExample.source:
(defclass animal ()
  ((name :initarg :name :accessor name)))

(defgeneric speak (a))
(defmethod speak ((a animal))
  (format t "~a makes a sound.~%" (name a)))

(speak (make-instance 'animal :name "Rex"))
